📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After a string of tech outages and hacks, many Americans are on alert. And on Thursday, the Wall Street Journal reported that a ransomware group had leaked the data of thousands of customers at JPMorgan Chase, Mastercard, and Visa.

Crucially, all of the companies have said that no credit card numbers or customer funds were compromised in the cyberattack. The companies' financial services are all operating normally, and JPMorgan Chase released a statement on X confirming the hack is unrelated to a Chase Bank outage earlier this week.

The leak contained some customers' names and email addresses, according to JPMorgan Chase.

According to recent reports, for its part, a Mastercard representative told Mashable that the incident "resulted in the exposure of a limited amount of email addresses — non-payments information — from a small subset of cardholders enrolled in a specific benefit program." Customers can continue to use their cards as normal. The spokesperson added, "At this time, the exposure has been contained and our teams are working with the provider to support the impacted cardholders as needed." SOCRadar, a cybersecurity and threat analysis tech giant, reported that the Russian ransomware group n0n claimed responsibility for the hack. Not only that, but SOCRadar found that n0n has also claimed to have compromised data at major organizations including Airbnb, Starbucks, EssilorLuxottica, Procter & Gamble, Walmart, and AARP — all in the past three days.

However, just because a hacking group claims responsibility for an attack, that doesn't mean that an attack occurred.

Apple fires back at Epic over claims it withheld 122,000 documents

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Apple has responded to Epic Games’ filing from last Friday, pushing back against accusations that it improperly withheld more than 122,000 documents related to its proposed App Store commissions.
  • While the Supreme Court is set to review whether the civil contempt designation against Apple should be upheld in its lawsuit against Epic Games, the two companies have also been battling in the district court over what commission, if any, Apple should be allowed to charge on purchases made through external payment systems.
  • Apple submitted its proposal to the district court on August 13, calling for commissions ranging from 5% to 15%, but Epic is disputing not just the basis for those proposed rates, but also Apple’s handling of document production in the proceedings.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Apple has responded to Epic Games’ filing from last Friday, pushing back against accusations that it improperly withheld more than 122,000 documents related to its proposed App Store commissions. Here are the details.

While the Supreme Court is set to review whether the civil contempt designation against Apple should be upheld in its lawsuit against Epic Games, the two companies have also been battling in the district court over what commission, if any, Apple should be allowed to charge on purchases made through external payment systems.

Apple submitted its proposal to the district court on August 13, calling for commissions ranging from 5% to 15%, but Epic is disputing not just the basis for those proposed rates, but also Apple’s handling of document production in the proceedings.

As part of the proceedings, Epic had submitted 16 categories of documents it wanted Apple to produce (including “internal analyses of the financial or business impact” of its proposed commissions and “communications relating to any strategies to dissuade developers from offering link-outs”), along with a list of current and former Apple employees whose records should be searched.

Apple agreed to use Epic’s proposed search terms and include all employees, and began producing documents it determined were responsive to Epic’s requests.

Epic, however, mentioned last Friday that Apple was improperly withholding more than 122,000 documents matching those search terms from the records of the seven initial employees, and asked the court to order Apple to produce all matching non-privileged documents, regardless of its relevance assessments.

Which brings us to Apple’s newest filing.

In its filing, Apple argues that contrary to Epic’s claim that its proposed search terms were “tailored” to the proceedings over link-out fees, they were actually “overbroad,” capturing large numbers of unrelated documents.

For instance, Apple notes that while intended to identify documents related to its proposed commission rates, Epic’s “commission*” search term also “captures documents that refer to government and private commissions, as well as documents hitting on the totally irrelevant term ‘commissioner,’ such as documents discussing the NFL Commissioner.”.

“[…] the use of a wildcard in a search string is designated by the asterisk symbol, which means that the search string will hit on any term that includes the prefix before the asterisk.

In the same vein, Apple notes that “Epic’s use of ‘fee*’ in its search strings related to litigation and Apple’s link-out-related projects pulled in documents containing words like ‘feel,’ ‘feed,’ ‘feedback,’ ‘feet,’ and ‘feeble’ without the word ‘fee’ or ‘fees’ appearing at all.”.

Apple’s overall argument is that these unrelated matches account for the vast majority of documents identified by Epic’s searches, and it cites legal precedent to argue that it should only be required to produce documents responsive to Epic’s requests, rather than every document matching the agreed-upon search terms:.

In fact, at least 95% of the Initial Custodian Document Population hit on generic terms like these and did not include any reference to the term “link-out” or its variations, despite that concept being central to the Proffer and related discovery. These sweeping terms do not just increase the total volume of the Initial Custodian Document Population, they also captured highly sensitive and irrelevant documents, such as Apple employees’ personal tax or financial records, medical records, documents discussing unannounced products, documents containing passwords, investor-relations materials, and privileged or protected legal communications.

Industry observers note that the law is clear: parties are only required to produce responsive documents, not every document returned by a search string. […] (“The Court will not compel defendants to produce any document simply because it contains a search term whether or not it is responsive to the discovery request.”). Epic has not shown, and cannot show, why the regular discovery process should be disrupted here. Speculation based on hit counts, particularly where the producing party can explain low responsiveness rates, does not justify the extraordinary and unprecedented remedy Epic seeks.

Apple goes on to argue that complying with Epic’s demands would require extensive additional work, including reviewing documents for privileged or sensitive information and redacting protected material, making it impossible to meet Epic’s proposed December 2 deadline.

Finally, Apple asks the court to reject Epic’s motion but proposes that, should the court decide that some intervention is warranted, a randomized, statistically significant sample of the documents it deems nonresponsive be submitted to a Special Master for independent review, rather than producing all of them to Epic directly.

The game only offers a first-person perspective in very limited circumstances.

It has been revealed that grand Theft Auto 6 gives players lots of ways to customize the experience, from the clothes the protagonists wear to granular user interface controls. Being able to shift your perspective of the action is part of that. Rockstar has long offered GTA players the ability to reposition the camera, and you can do that this time around as well.

In the camera tab of the settings menu, you can adjust the height of the camera while you're on foot, as well as the horizontal and vertical follow speeds. You have similar options for land and water vehicles, along with specific follow speeds based on whether you're the driver or a passenger. When it comes to aircraft, you can adjust the follow speed and determine whether the camera follows your plane when you do a barrel roll.

It has been revealed that when you're out there exploring the map in a land or water vehicle, you can change the height of the camera on the fly. To switch between the three options, hold the down button on the D-pad, pick the height you want and confirm. You'll also be able to switch to the cinematic camera mode here. This makes things like high-speed chases look cool, but you might find it harder to steer your vehicle.

In addition, there are some very limited ways in which you can switch to a first-person perspective. While you're on foot, you can hold the left trigger on your controller and click the right thumbstick. This lets you take a closer look at your surroundings.

Sources indicate that going back to the camera section of the settings menu, you can enable a first-person perspective when your character is looking at their phone. If you look at your phone while you're driving (in GTA 6, never in real life), you'll see your device and the road from a first-person view as well. Perhaps Rockstar will add a proper first-person mode to GTA 6 down the line, as it did with the previous game.

Tech Report: UK government forced to disclose secret Apple backdoor order

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • government has been ordered to confirm that it issued a secret order demanding Apple to provide authorities with encrypted customer information.
  • The Thursday ruling from the U.K.’s Investigatory Powers Tribunal, an independent court that allows citizens to challenge government surveillance orders, is a rare rebuke for the government, which sought to keep the encryption backdoor order a state secret.
  • The tribunal’s ruling rejected the Home Office’s claim that disclosing the order would be damaging to national security.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that the U.K. government has been ordered to confirm that it issued a secret order demanding Apple to provide authorities with encrypted customer information.

The Thursday ruling from the U.K.’s Investigatory Powers Tribunal, an independent court that allows citizens to challenge government surveillance orders, is a rare rebuke for the government, which sought to keep the encryption backdoor order a state secret.

The tribunal’s ruling rejected the Home Office’s claim that disclosing the order would be damaging to national security.

Industry observers note that the ruling comes a year after the U.K. government reportedly demanded that Apple build a backdoor to allow U.K. authorities access to customer data anywhere in the world. Details of the so-called “technical capabilities notice,” which are issued under strict non-disclosure rules, leaked to the media, which drew ire from White House officials and U.S. lawmakers who criticized the effort, arguing that the U.K. order would put Americans’ privacy at risk.

In a recent development, california-based Apple refused the order, and blocked U.K. users from switching on its Advanced Data Protection data-encryption feature for iCloud, rather than comply with the demand. The U.K.’s secret order was later narrowed to allow access to British nationals’ data stored in Apple’s encrypted cloud, and Apple also challenged this second order.

Industry observers note that prior to the ruling, Apple was legally barred from disclosing the order, even after details leaked. When reached for comment, Apple told TechCrunch that it welcomes the decision to make public the fact that the U.K. Home Office issued a technical capability notice.

Apple previously mentioned that it has “never built a backdoor or master key” to any of its products or services and “never will.”.

A spokesperson for the U.K. Home Office, which has yet to confirm the existence of a notice, did not respond to a request for comment.

Rights group Liberty International, which brought the legal challenge on behalf of two individuals, stated that this is the first known time that the government has been compelled to confirm the existence of a secret technical order.

A final hearing on what specific order details can be released is anticipated next year.

#1529. Google Built a Giant ‘Mirror Dimension’ Internet to Test Its Chrome AI Agents

Google Built a Giant ‘Mirror Dimension’ Internet to Test Its Chrome AI Agents

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (645 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: WIRED

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, as the Google Chrome team has worked to develop AI browsing features using the manufacturer's Gemini models, they realized they need to go the extra mile to keep things from going haywire.
  • Industry observers note that “Web-use” agents need to be familiar with the open internet, how to navigate real websites and platforms, and how to be hardened against web attacks.
  • The “Mirror Dimension,” which Google is detailing in a blog post today for the first time, is a sweeping and diverse but isolated web ecosystem that the Chrome team entirely controls.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, as the Google Chrome team has worked to develop AI browsing features using the manufacturer's Gemini models, they realized they need to go the extra mile to keep things from going haywire. So they did the only thing they could think to do—they built an expansive alternate-universe internet that they completely control.

Industry observers note that “Web-use” agents need to be familiar with the open internet, how to navigate real websites and platforms, and how to be hardened against web attacks. So training them in limited test environments is only so effective. Plus, models can develop what's known as “eval awareness,” where they behave differently because they have determined that they are in a test or simulation. On the other hand, setting unrefined agents loose on the open internet is a bad idea. That’s where the alternate-universe internet comes in.

The “Mirror Dimension,” which Google is detailing in a blog post today for the first time, is a sweeping and diverse but isolated web ecosystem that the Chrome team entirely controls. It includes a vast array of websites and platforms—including social media sites, shopping, and bank dashboards—that are built with all the components and attributes of real websites. Browsing assistant agents must interact with the sites and complete tasks in Chrome the way they would on the real internet. And they face resilience tests as they go, like hidden prompt-injection attacks, to test their defenses.

“Agents are not programmed, so you can’t predict every possible thing an agent might see; the exploration space that we have to address is huge, and the web is hostile,” says Charles Qian, a software engineer on the Chrome AI security team. “Any user can ask any prompt on any website, so we really need to explore that space as thoroughly as we can. And we’ve seen the agent start to develop a mature sense of judgment when it comes to knowing what information is actually needed for a task and when to punt back to the user for a confirmation.”.

Building out and populating the Mirror Dimension was a challenge in itself, because it needed to be vast and varied enough to represent the scale of the real web while being developed promptly. To construct it, the Chrome team gathered armies of website and web app development agents guided by a purpose-built AI harness to quickly create realistic web services and data flows—down to details like entering promo codes on a shopping site or populating social media pages.

Recent findings suggest that even though the entire environment is controlled by Google, Chrome is built with so many user protections and validity checks that, in order to allow the agents to use real Chrome (which is crucial for accurate training), the researchers essentially had to hack the browser and take elaborate steps like making forged web certificates for validity checks so the agents could have a normal experience. The team emphasizes, though, that none of these attacks would be possible against regular Chrome customers on the open internet. They were all facilitated by the god-mode-type access and privilege the team inherently has because they control the entire environment and network.

The researchers say that while the browsing assistant agents they have been testing are benign and do not have cyber capabilities, their goal is to make the Mirror Dimension available to teams across Google so more researchers have access to the safe and controlled environment for testing.

“We’re sharing this approach so other teams both internally and externally think about doing it this way,” states Doug Turner, Google’s director of engineering. “This is the first step; there’s going to be continued investment in this approach to train models. And I would imagine as they become more sophisticated, we’ll have to continue working on this environment to make it more and more realistic.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Tax software maker Intuit remarked Thursday that it has agreed to sell marketing subsidiary Mailchimp to Italian technology consolidator Bending Spoons for $3.68 billion in cash and stock.
  • The sale is a costly retreat for Intuit, which paid $12 billion for Mailchimp in 2021 in a push beyond its core tax and accounting businesses.
  • The deal is the latest instance of Bending Spoons picking up a once promising technology asset.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tax software maker Intuit remarked Thursday that it has agreed to sell marketing subsidiary Mailchimp to Italian technology consolidator Bending Spoons for $3.68 billion in cash and stock. The deal is set to close in early 2027, according to a statement.

The sale is a costly retreat for Intuit, which paid $12 billion for Mailchimp in 2021 in a push beyond its core tax and accounting businesses. Five years later, the software maker is unloading the email-marketing tech giant for less than one-third of that price after Mailchimp became a drag on its overall revenue growth.

The deal is the latest instance of Bending Spoons picking up a once promising technology asset. The company bought productivity software startup Airtable in September for 10% of what it was once worth.

The Bending Spoons portfolio also contains AOL, Brightcove, Eventbrite, Evernote, Meetup, Vimeo, and WeTransfer.

In August Intuit started running Mailchimp as a distinct operating segment. The move was meant to give investors more transparency as the company tried to manage the unit for profitability, Sandeep Aujla, Intuit's finance chief, noted at a September company briefing.

Sources indicate that also on Thursday, Intuit confirmed stronger-than-expected earnings and revenue for its fiscal first quarter, which ended on Oct. 31. The organization reported $2.91 in adjusted earnings per share on $4.35 billion in revenue. Analysts polled by LSEG were looking for $2.70 per share and $4.31 billion in revenue.

It has been revealed that while Intuit's revenue increased 12% year over year, Mailchimp revenue declined 1% to $313 million. Analysts polled by StreetAccount had expected $314.4 million.

According to recent reports, management called for $22.88 to $23.12 in adjusted earnings per share for the 2027 fiscal year, with $23.081 billion to $23.365 billion in revenue. Analysts polled by LSEG had predicted $23.62 in adjusted earnings per share on $23.43 billion in revenue. Intuit shares tumbled 15% in extended trading.

Sources indicate that the company noted Mailchimp should produce $1.256 billion to $1.266 billion in fiscal 2027 revenue, which would be down 1% to flat year over year. In August Aujla said Intuit anticipated Mailchimp's higher effective prices offsetting increased client churn. Mailchimp was founded in 2001. Rivals include Klaviyo, which went public in 2023.

Berkshire Hathaway invested $600 million in Bending Spoons when the acquirer went public in July, and in October Bending Spoons said Berkshire invested another $330 million.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, influencers are now able to link their Amazon and Instagram accounts to promote products. Some are concerned about what they’re opting in to.﻿.

Recent findings suggest that influencers are now able to link their Amazon and Instagram accounts to promote products. Some are concerned about what they’re opting in to.﻿.

For years, influencers have come up with workarounds on social media to figure out how to share affiliate links with followers. A new integration between Instagram and Amazon was announced earlier this month as a way to make it easier for influencers to make money from affiliate links — but some content creators are suspicious about who really benefits.

According to recent reports, the fresh integration allows creators to connect their Instagram and Amazon accounts and automatically tag products with their affiliate links, from which they earn a commission when followers make purchases. Influencers will be able to embed up to 30 product links in a Reel or 20 in a feed post, but a permissions setting has led to concerns about what creators are actually agreeing to.

In connecting an Amazon account, creators must agree to allow the retailer and its brand sellers to create ads from “any public content” that includes a related affiliate link. Influencers must also agree to acknowledge that brands can edit their content and use their “testimonial, caption or media” for ads.

Sources indicate that the wide-ranging permissions are giving creators pause. Some have urged peers not to connect their accounts without reviewing the permissions and understanding how the feature would affect earnings. People making money on social media spend years tweaking their content and strategy to maximize reach, engagement, and, by extension, their bottom line. For some, it appeared that they would be giving Amazon and its sellers the ability to use their content under unclear terms. On Instagram head Adam Mosseri’s post announcing the feature, influencers complained about the lack of clarity, questioned whether using the feature would decrease their reach (which some creators say happens when they link to outside products), and demanded answers to whether their commission rate would stay the same when Amazon or brands use their content for ads.

Linking products through the new integration won’t reduce reach, Jimmy O’Keefe, Instagram’s director of product marketing, mentioned in an email to The Verge. O’Keefe also noted that creators will continue to earn commission through affiliate links when Amazon boosts their posts, and that they can stop the boosting in settings or disconnect the integration entirely. There’s also a separate, manual way to add products without linking accounts, if a creator wants to opt out of having their content made into ads.

It has been revealed that amazon has an enormous influencer program that reaches across social media platforms. It is so lucrative that some content creators are able to make a living almost exclusively by hawking products for sale on Amazon, building empires on the shopping habits of their followers. When it comes to putting those links in front of followers, though, social platforms have historically been a roadblock, hence the cottage industry of link-in-bio tools meant to circumvent limits. Slowly but surely, though, platforms like Instagram, Facebook, and YouTube — perhaps chasing the success of TikTok Shop — have added more and more shopping features. The result is that shopping and social media begin to feel more and more like the same thing.

#1524. You won't find this fan favorite feature in GTA 6

You won't find this fan favorite feature in GTA 6

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, some of the more hardcore fans, running on little-to-no sleep, might be working their way through the missions in the Grand Theft Auto 6.
  • Even after more than 100 hours playing the game for his review, GamesRadar editor-in-chief Josh West remarked that he found no replay option.
  • Mission replay was first added to The Ballad of Gay Tony, the second Grand Theft Auto 4 expansion, back in 2009.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Replaying missions is possible, but not easy.

In a recent development, some of the more hardcore fans, running on little-to-no sleep, might be working their way through the missions in the Grand Theft Auto 6. Unlike in its predecessor though, GTA 6 has no option to replay completed story missions. That marks a major change from the previous game, which allowed players to run back finished mission from the pause menu, mostly to retry its skill challenges. (Those haven't reappeared, either.).

Even after more than 100 hours playing the game for his review, GamesRadar editor-in-chief Josh West remarked that he found no replay option. Other early-access reviewers are reporting the same. So, the only way back into a mission, at least for now, is to load a manual save made before it started, and before autosave overwrites itself.

Mission replay was first added to The Ballad of Gay Tony, the second Grand Theft Auto 4 expansion, back in 2009. It also introduced a scoring system that graded players on secondary mission goals like completion time, damage taken and headshots. Replay was introduced essentially so players could go back and get a better score. Then, with GTA 5, those goals became bronze, silver and gold medals, and achievements tied to attaining them. Rockstar's Red Dead Redemption 2's also had a "Gold Rush" trophy, which also asked for 70 gold medals out of the 104 available via its story missions.

Recent findings suggest that GTA 6 has no gold medal objectives at all, at least as things stand now. Instead, challenges can be found in their own section of the progress menu. They cover broader goals rather than being mission-specific, and mostly unlock cheats once the story is completed. Rockstar North's co-studio head Rob Nelson told IGN that Rockstar had made "a very conscious effort to open things up where possible" in GTA 6's missions. Players will now find that some missions suggest an optimal route that players can ignore, for example, with the job turning into a police chase rather than ending in failure.

Industry observers note that red Dead Redemption 2 players long complained that straying from set paths could fail missions. That, along with GTA 5's mission medals enforcing a linear playstyle, seems to be the reason why Rockstar left them out.

Industry observers note that GTA 6 gives us 15 save slots. That might seem generous on the face of it, but it's not all that many for a campaign that has more than 90 main missions. Sharper minds than I have worked out that keeping a route back to everything would mean a fresh manual save roughly every 6.6 percent of the way through the game.

The missing mission repeat feature probably comes down to how sprawling GTA 6's story is. Entire missions can play out differently based on decisions players made earlier, sometimes without knowing they were making them. A heist, for example, can be buttery smooth or turn into an awful mess depending on gameplay completed hours earlier. Story choices also shape the wider world, down to which characters live and die. Reloading a mission and playing it in isolation would ignore the choices that set it up originally.

It's not all bad news: Races, stunts, pool and other minigames are repeatable, as are shop robberies and the bank jobs as the story unlocks. Robbed locations gray out on the map and reset after a cooldown.

And obviously GTA 6's story was designed to support repeat playthroughs, but that's a significant commitment. Nelson himself — the game's lead dev — has said his playthrough took 80 hours, covering the main story and some optional goals. In GTA 5, you could jump back into a favorite mission in a few minutes, but now, playing one differently means planning saves in advance or committing to another full run. Whether that changes remains to be seen.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Canva today declared “AI Controls,” a upcoming toggle that completely turns off generative AI features within the editing app.
  • Generative AI can be quite helpful in working on posters, editing images, and more, but it’s not everyone’s preference.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that AI has taken over everything in the past few years, with AI features bombarding virtually every app or service available. If you’ve ever wanted to just turn off AI features, Canva proves that it could be a simple toggle, if companies actually wanted to give you a choice.

Canva today declared “AI Controls,” a upcoming toggle that completely turns off generative AI features within the editing app.

Generative AI can be quite helpful in working on posters, editing images, and more, but it’s not everyone’s preference. Canva puts this well:.

For some people, AI is the most exciting creative tool in a generation, while others prefer bringing their ideas to life without it. We believe the future of creativity should give everyone the freedom to choose their own path, whether that’s creating with AI, without it, or somewhere in between.

In a recent development, to give its customers the choice, Canva’s Permissions menu now has a simple toggle for “Enable Generative AI features.” Toggling it off disables features such as Magic Write and Magic Edit. There’s also an option to limit how much AI-generated imagery appears in the Canva library.

Put simply, this is great to see.

According to recent reports, AI has its place, but everyone should have a choice like this, especially when it comes to apps and services used for artistry in the same vein as Canva. Yet, the tech industry continues to go in the opposite direction, shoving AI into every corner whether it’s actually useful or not. Canva proves, though, that it doesn’t have to be that way.

#1519. Tech Report: Apple HomePod mini 2 review: A necessary, but underwhelming enhancement

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1531 w)
📖 Baca
Gadgets ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Engadget ↗ Open Full Page

Tech Report: Apple HomePod mini 2 review: A necessary, but underwhelming enhancement

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1531 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Engadget

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • I'd be willing to forgive you if you forgot about the new HomePod mini.
  • The most notable update on the HomePod mini 2 is on the inside.
  • In a recent development, the recently updated assistant isn't all the S10 is helping with here.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I'd be willing to forgive you if you forgot about the new HomePod mini. The overhauled smart speaker played a supporting role at best during Apple's Welcome Home event last month, behind the HomeView, and probably, in some minds, behind the updated Apple TV 4K. Still, the tech giant provides a few upgrades in the HomePod mini 2 ($149), ensuring that it's ready for Siri AI and the assistant's newfound ability to offer personalized context for your queries. The main problem? The speaker doesn't yet support the recently upgraded virtual assistant Apple spent years improving.

The most notable update on the HomePod mini 2 is on the inside. Apple swapped in its S10 chip from the Apple Watch Series 10, kicking the nearly antique S5 silicon to the curb. For a Watch comparison, that's like going from a Series 5 or first-gen Watch SE, which debuted in 2019 and 2020 respectively, to the 2024 edition. It's a substantial leap, and it's one Apple says was necessary for the HomePod mini to work with Siri AI.

In a recent development, the recently updated assistant isn't all the S10 is helping with here. Apple states the component can run real-time music evaluation "to optimize dynamic range, loudness and acoustic performance," with a hand from "advanced computational analysis." When connected to the newly introduced fourth-gen Apple TV 4K, you can use four HomePod mini 2 speakers as a surround sound setup. That S10 chip helps the speakers recognize their positions in a room and adjust the lag, convey that info to Apple's streaming box, and audio levels accordingly.

In a recent development, I only have two HomePod mini 2s, so I wasn't able to test this configuration, but I did hear it during Apple's event in October. Even with that brief experience, I can tell you using two second-gen HomePods as the front speakers and two HomePod minis as the rears is a much better setup. The HomePod mini doesn't muster enough bass to be a great home theater speaker on its own, and those full-size HomePods bring the boom when an action scene demands it.

Before now, you could send audio from a Mac to a HomePod mini, but Apple has expanded the functionality so that the second-gen model can serve as persistent default speakers. This means, in theory, they'll stay connected to your Mac as the primary output rather than just relying on a temporary AirPlay link. This allows you to use the HomePod mini 2, or a pair of them, for everything on your computer — from FaceTime calls to games — without having to think about connecting each app or session to the speaker(s).

The HomePod line has always had lights on the top, but they haven't really done much. Before now, the top touch panel would light up if audio was playing or display an animation when you chatted with Siri. With a latest feature called Sound Glow, those lights now show hues that compliment a song's album artwork. The lights move in real time, reacting to the bass and treble in each tune. If you opt for a soundscape, Sound Glow reacts to that too, showing an animation that resembles the pitter patter of rain drops, for example. It isn't a game-changing feature, but it's a nice use of lighting that was barely utilized previously.

According to recent reports, lastly, there are the new colors. The HomePod mini 2 comes in pink, green, blue, white and midnight (dark grey), with those first three coordinating well with Apple's iMac colors. That list means the company retired orange and yellow from the previous generation, both of which looked great in their time. As you can see, my review units are green, and I've enjoyed the pop of color they've added to my desk over the last few weeks.

In a recent development, given that Apple saw fit to bestow a "2" on this HomePod mini, I expected some upgrades to overall sound quality to be in the mix. Unfortunately, I can't notice a difference between old and fresh models. Sometimes I think there's some variation, but it's not substantial enough that I'm sure, and it's not consistent across various musical styles. I do like the audio performance of the HomePod mini for its size, but it still has a sound profile of crisp highs and prominent mids offset by bass tone that lacks dynamics and depth. It's good enough for casual listening or background tunes, but not for anything more than that.

Recent findings suggest that despite the lack of Siri AI, I was hoping the S10 chip would provide a performance boost for the old Siri experience you have to settle for right now. However, the assistant's responses to basic questions took the same amount of time as they do on the first-gen model. To be clear, they're quick on both devices, I'm merely pointing out there's no difference in this regard. Just don't try to ask the old assistant to dive into Apple's core apps for you, or try to have an on-going conversation — neither request will bear any fruit.

Industry observers note that the biggest issue with the HomePod mini 2 right now is its biggest omission: Siri AI. The recently updated assistant isn't available on the speaker yet, and Apple hasn't provided a timeline for its arrival either. The upgraded HomePod mini is equipped to support the now-current-gen Siri, thanks to the S10 chip. However, you'll have to wait for Siri's newfound contextual awareness to dive into your Messages, Calendar and other apps on your iPhone or iPad. And to me, that's a huge miss for Apple on an overhauled smart speaker. You'll also have to wait for the more conversational chats with Siri as the HomePod mini 2 doesn't yet support those either.

I like the idea of using a HomePod mini 2 or a stereo pair of them as a persistent computer speaker with a Mac, but it's not a great experience in practice. Any time you do anything — start a song, pause a song, skip tracks — there's a 1-2 second delay in the audio responding. The lights on the top of the speakers, including the Sound Glow effect, will stop shining immediately, but the audio has to catch up. There's also a slight delay between speakers if you're using a stereo pair, which sounds like every song has added reverb. For these reasons, I found the Mac speaker feature more frustrating than enjoyable, and I quickly moved back to AirPlay over a nearby Sonos speaker for my productivity tunes. And I haven't even mentioned the fact that I can't get the persistent connection to stick with my MacBook Air either. I'm constantly reselecting the HomePod mini 2 as the audio output.

Industry observers note that another item that's disappointing is something else that's not here: a substantial overhaul. The original HomePod mini is six years old at this point, so I expected a much bigger redesign for the second-gen version (until the rumor mill squashed that). If you have a first-gen HomePod mini, you'll miss out on the updated Siri, whenever it arrives, and newly introduced features like Sound Glow and the home theater option. And if you're hoping to create a stereo pair, you'll need two of the same generation HomePod minis to do that; you can't pair a first-gen speaker with a second-gen model for that purpose.

In a recent development, lastly, there's the price. The previous version was $99 before Apple raised it to $129 in June when the manufacturer hiked the prices on pretty much all of its hardware. Now, I'm well aware of the global economic factors at play, especially the AI-fueled cost increase on RAM and other components, but asking $50 more than the first-gen model for incremental updates is tough. Had Apple kept the price at the June rate, the HomePod mini 2 would be a much easier recommendation.

In a recent development, it's baffling to me that Apple would announce an updated HomePod mini without support for the latest version of Siri ready to go. The speaker's primary use is a hands-free conduit to the company's voice assistant, after all. The only decent conclusion I can come to is that Apple wanted to announce what it considered was a full suite of home products around the HomeView debut, and it felt like the Apple TV 4K, HomePod mini and a collection of smart home devices were the best way to do that. I would be interested to know what the hold up is, because the Apple Watch Series 10 supports Siri AI already, and those wearables are also running the same S10 chip as the HomePod mini 2. But, of course, Apple isn't talking specifics.

After spending a few weeks with the HomePod mini 2, I mostly wish Apple had just waited. At a higher price, this isn't as compelling as it used to be in terms of getting Siri in your home. And with Siri AI missing, and some of the fresh audio features proving to be unreliable, it's clear a bit more polish was needed here.

The problem with strong passwords isn’t understanding why you need them; it’s keeping track of a different one for every account.

That’s useful whether you’re creating an account for a single purchase or signing into a service you use every day.

Unique passwords also help limit the fallout from a data breach. If a retailer exposes your login credentials, using a different password elsewhere means those same credentials won’t unlock your other accounts.

With unlimited logins and encrypted vaults that sync across devices, Proton Pass lets you keep those details together as you move between your phone and computer.

According to recent reports, proton Pass is available for practically every platform, from Chrome and Firefox on the web to native macOS, Windows, and Linux apps to, of course, iOS and Android. This makes it trivially easy to access your passwords, passkeys, and API credentials wherever you find yourself.

Black Friday shopping often leaves something behind long after the packages arrive: a steady stream of promotional emails from stores you barely remember visiting.

Proton Pass includes unlimited hide-my-email aliases, giving you an alternative to handing out your real address every time you create an account.

According to recent reports, an alias is an extra email address that forwards messages to your normal inbox. You can give it to a shopping website and still receive your order confirmations and delivery updates, without sharing the underlying address you use for everything else.

Recent findings suggest that if that alias starts receiving spam, you can switch it off. Your real email address stays the same, and you don’t have to enhancement all your other accounts.

It’s a practical way to put some distance between your primary inbox and the websites you’re trying for the first time. A separate alias for each service also gives you more control: you can stop messages arriving through one address without disrupting the others.

Passwords are only part of what’s worth keeping in a secure, accessible place.

In a recent development, proton Pass also stores notes, credit card details, and other confidential information in end-to-end encrypted vaults. That makes it useful for the small, everyday moments when you need something sensitive and don’t want to go looking for it.

When you’re booking a flight, saved passport details let you look up the information you need without digging through a drawer halfway through the reservation.

When you’re shopping online, saved card details mean you don’t have to leave the checkout page to find your wallet.

Industry observers note that when you’re traveling, keeping a digital copy of an notable document within reach gives you a convenient reference while you’re away from home. It doesn’t replace an original document where one is required, but it can save you from searching through scattered files and messages.

Industry observers note that pass Plus also includes a built-in two-factor authenticator, Dark Web Monitoring, and secure link and vault sharing. Those features give you more ways to manage access to your accounts and share sensitive information when you need to.

Pass Plus is the straightforward choice for one person who wants password generation, autofill, unlimited aliases, and secure storage.

In a recent development, pass Family includes six Pass Plus accounts and a family admin panel. If several people in your household need a password manager, it’s worth considering rather than setting everyone up with separate subscriptions.

Proton Unlimited bundles Pass with Proton VPN, Proton Mail, Proton Drive, and more, including 500 GB of cloud storage. It’s the option to consider if you also want a VPN, encrypted email, and cloud storage alongside your password manager.

A password manager isn’t the most conspicuous Black Friday purchase, but it’s one you can put to work immediately: the next account you create, the next password you forget, or the next time a checkout asks for details you don’t have handy.

Proton’s offers are available to new people and include a 30-day money-back guarantee.

In a recent development, few things could generate more buzz for a small restaurant than a visit from Jensen Huang. In recent years, the former Nvidia CEO became known for dining out at street markets and hole-in-the-wall noodle joints across Asia, drawing huge crowds of fans and photographers wherever he went.

But after Huang resigned last week amid revelations of multiple extramarital affairs, some of the food vendors he helped put on the map are wondering whether their most famous customer is still good for business. In Taiwan, where Huang was born and his dining habits have long been a spectator sport, many say they aren't ready to turn against their hometown hero.

Tu Chang-chun, the owner of Ice World, a shaved-ice shop in Taipei, describes Huang as friendly, the kind of person who puts others around him at ease. His impression of the billionaire hasn’t changed since he learned of his affair with Alice Huang, a businesswoman accused of spying for China.

Sources indicate that “It’s not as if he killed someone or set something on fire. Why blow it all out of proportion?” Tu said on Monday evening, standing beneath the yellow lights of his stall at Linjiang Street Night Market. “Now, a lot of foreigners walk past, see my sign, and laugh. People just love kicking someone when they’re down.”.

Sources indicate that at the entrance of his shop, Tu continues to proudly display a photo of Huang posing with him and his wife. “I think he’s such a warm and approachable person,” Tu added. “Why are people treating him this way?”.

Jensen Huang has visited this shaved ice stall at Taipei’s Linjiang Street Night Market three times since 2023.

Tu says that Huang has visited his shop three times since 2023, and he always orders the same thing: mango shaved ice with tangyuan (sticky rice balls). The dessert, a blend of tropical fruit and condensed milk, is popular in Taipei’s bustling night markets, especially among first-time visitors to the island.

Recent findings suggest that “When he came in for shaved ice, he would spend half an hour eating a single bowl,” recalled Tu. “Whenever someone came up to take a photo with him, he got right up. He’s not pretentious.”.

At a tofu pudding shop near Ningxia Night Market in western Taipei, photos of Huang remain on display alongside those of other prominent technology figures who have visited, including Morris Chang, the founder of Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Organization (TSMC). The store manager, Hsieh, defended the shop’s decision to keep them up.

“I don’t think this changes the fact that he’s a very successful businessman,” Hsieh said of Huang’s affairs with Alice Huang and other women. “Having an affair is a private matter.”.

Hsieh, who agreed to be identified only by his surname for privacy reasons, mentioned that Huang had visited the shop four times over the past few years, and on each occasion he seemed friendly and down-to-earth.

Owner Tu Chang-chun remarked he has no looks to take down photos Jensen Huang visiting his shaved-ice shop.

In Taiwan, Huang’s culinary indulgences extended well beyond street food. He frequented some of Taipei’s most exclusive restaurants, where he hosted technology executives for what became known in the local press as “Trillion-Dollar Banquets,” a reference to the attendees’ combined net worth of more than 1 trillion Newly introduced Taiwan dollars.

Sources indicate that the dinners often drew crowds of journalists and photographers hoping to catch a glimpse of Huang and his guests. The intense media attention helps explain why so many photographs and videos of Huang with Alice Huang were captured in Taiwan. Restaurant owners, meanwhile, welcomed the publicity, often proudly displaying photographs of themselves with Huang inside their establishments.

But not every food vendor has rallied to Huang’s defense. Some have removed advertisements or photos featuring him, while others have tried to capitalize on the scandal to generate publicity. A night market vendor in Taipei told Taiwanese media that he was considering taking down advertisements associated with Huang out of concern that they could hurt his business.

The Taiwanese tea chain 19 Tea House debuted a newly introduced drink this week, giving it a name that pokes fun at Huang’s alleged “womanizing” ways. According to the chain, the drink combines osmanthus-infused honey with fresh lemon, offering a blend of fragrant floral notes and sweet-and-tangy citrus flavors.

Support for Huang in Taiwan has also extended far beyond the restaurants he frequented. On Monday evening, Taipei 101, the island’s iconic skyscraper just blocks from one of Huang’s favorite night markets, lit up with messages of support for the former Nvidia CEO, including “Taiwan ♡ Jensen,” “Family ♡ Friendship,” “Thrive Together,” and “Taiwan AI Build Future Together.”.

Tech industry figures who supported the initiative told Taiwan’s state-run Central News Agency that the illumination campaign was intended to “help restore Jensen Huang’s reputation,” urging the public not to “kick him when he's down, but instead offer warmth and support during the autumn and winter.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • This is part of Project Suncatcher, an experiment aimed at running AI systems in space.
  • Recent findings suggest that google has partnered up with Jeff Bezos' Blue Origin to deploy small satellite data centers into space, as part of its Project Suncatcher project.
  • Sources indicate that the rocket will carry several Google tensor processing units, the manufacturer's proprietary AI chips, along with data center servers.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This is part of Project Suncatcher, an experiment aimed at running AI systems in space.

Recent findings suggest that google has partnered up with Jeff Bezos' Blue Origin to deploy small satellite data centers into space, as part of its Project Suncatcher project. Each of these satellites will be equipped with "roughly the capacity of a data center rack" and will enter into a sun-synchronous orbit via heavy-lift New Glenn rockets.

Sources indicate that the rocket will carry several Google tensor processing units, the manufacturer's proprietary AI chips, along with data center servers. The first launch isn't scheduled until early 2029, so we have a couple of years to see if this whole project even works.

Blue Origin and Google have entered into a launch services agreement for Project Suncatcher, Google's research moonshot exploring how an interconnected network of solar-powered satellites equipped with its AI chips, Tensor Processing Units (TPUs), could scale machine learning... pic.twitter.com/dUWuHR4Pla.

— Blue Origin (@blueorigin) November 19, 2026.

This is an experiment that Google calls a "long-term moonshot" to see if it's possible to put AI infrastructure in space by "tapping into the abundant solar power in orbit." The benefits of this would be massive. Data centers here on Earth are notorious hogs, with their snouts all over electricity grids, land and cooling systems.

Industry observers note that the hope is that the harsh vacuum of the cosmos will be a better fit for the technology. After all, in space nobody can hear you make endless industrial noises and high-pitched whirs all day every day. This is a very real situation for folks living near data centers.

Industry observers note that google is far from the only manufacturer trying to kick the data center can straight into outer space. Elon Musk's SpaceX has been experimenting with the idea, though it may involve putting a gigantic catapult on the moon (really.) There are also some startups fiddling with the technology, like Starcloud.

According to recent reports, can this even work? We don't know yet, though there are some serious hurdles to overcome. Google did deploy its first AI server satellite back in October, but it was sent into low-Earth orbit and can only operate for 15 minutes at a time. Scaling up the affiliated cooling systems looks to be incredibly difficult.

That's because standard heat dissipation doesn't work in space, so it has to be released through pipes and panels rather than conventional cooling systems. There's also the matter of radiation. It's everywhere and causes something called "bit flip." This essentially flips the binary code from a one to a zero, or vice versa. Obviously, this would be a major problem for binary-coded systems.

Did I mention the actual launches? It's extremely expensive to send stuff to space. Just one Falcon 9 launch costs around $74 million and the maximum payload can barely cover the hardware for a small server room, let alone a hyperscale data center.

"Expanding from one satellite to a vast network of them that operate like a giant data center will take years and enormous funds," Brandon Lucia, a professor of electrical and computer engineering at Carnegie Mellon University, told The New York Times. "If you do this on a large scale, there are additional engineering problems.".

According to recent reports, finally, there's a risk to us humans here on Earth. Scientists have been considering a theoretical scenario called Kessler syndrome for decades. This is when the density of objects in low-orbit gets so high and collisions become so commonplace that it creates a chain reaction of debris. We would be on the receiving end of that debris.

Industry observers note that this theory was posited back when there were just under 2,000 items circling a low-Earth orbit. That number has since risen to over 47,000 and Elon Musk recently floated an idea to add millions of latest satellites into the mix.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Google unveiled Android developer verification last year, and despite numerous objections from developers and customers, the firm is forging ahead. It began blocking the installation of unregistered apps in some countries this fall, and the system is expanding globally soon. Google says it will start rolling out the requirement in all regions in January 2027, and it urges devs who still haven’t registered their apps to do so soon.

The apps you download from the Play Store all come from verified developers, and Google’s newly introduced requirement expands that requirement to apps from third-party sources. Once developer verification is live in your region, you won’t be able to sideload apps unless the developer has registered with Google, which is framed as a security measure. Verification requires providing government identification and paying a $25 fee, which will allegedly make it harder for nefarious actors to distribute malware and scammy apps.

In September, Google launched verification in Brazil, Indonesia, Singapore, and Thailand. Apparently, nothing exploded, so the company is now ready to expand. It previously stated verification would go global in 2027, and it’s not wasting any time with the January start. It says that verification will reach all devices within “several months.”.

So far, Google is getting what it wanted from this initiative, with “millions” of non-Play apps already registered. The firm says this accounts for more than 99 percent of global Android app installs.

The verifier system service has already been rolled out to Google-certified devices running Android 8 Oreo or higher, which accounts for just about every Android device in the world outside of China and Russia. Google has also partnered with the biggest third-party app stores to enforce verification: Galaxy Store, Honor, Oppo, Xiaomi, Transsion, and Vivo. The system-level verifier is responsible for blocking installs, but these stores will only list verified apps once Google flips the switch.

Recent findings suggest that google has gotten a lot of feedback since announcing this change, and it has listened to some of it. Hobbyists will be able to register a free account to distribute apps to a small group. Google initially planned to limit this to 25 total installs, but that has since been increased to 50 installs. There’s also now an API that developers can use to streamline registering new application packages.

In a recent development, google also relented and created an opt-out system for users who don’t want their installations limited. The so-called “advanced flow” will let you install whatever you want regardless of verification status, but it’s not a simple toggle. The option will be buried, and there will be plenty of scary warnings about the risks. You’ll also have to wait 24 hours to fully activate the feature. This setting is already live, so you can tell your phone to ignore verification right now.

Industry observers note that even if Google has managed to make verification a little more warm and cuddly, it still gives the tech giant a lot more control. Developers in sanctioned nations won’t be able to verify their identities, locking them out of app distribution. Sideloading an app may also require a Google server connection. Only popular app IDs will be cached on devices for verification purposes. For others, your phone will have to check with Google before installing. These will be edge cases, certainly, but still very annoying ones.

As Google moves toward full verification enforcement, it has created guides for developers and app distributors to outline all the salient points. These guides suggest Google expects verification to be fully online by March 1, 2027.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Streaming services and social platforms are giving internet creators more places to make their next hit show. Disney+ is adding videos from TikTok creators, Netflix is expanding its lineup of creator-led podcasts, and Instagram is testing videos up to 90 minutes long.

But when it comes to what Americans watch on TV, YouTube is still king. In August, it accounted for a record 15.8 percent of U.S. TV watch time, more than twice Netflix’s 7.7 percent and the biggest share of any manufacturer in the rankings.

This week, YouTube gave us a look at what some of its biggest creators are making, from shows that are already live to those coming in the months ahead. Here's what’s on the slate.

Emma Chamberlain — What Are You Waiting For? Emma Chamberlain hates waiting in line, which makes her an especially good person to ask Upcoming Yorkers why they do it. The 2026 Mashable 101 honoree visits some of the city's busiest lines and talks to the people in them about what’s worth giving up part of their day for. The line is just the starting point for a closer look at the fandoms and subcultures that bring people together in person. The series, produced by Amplify Pictures, premieres on Chamberlain's channel in early 2027.

In a recent development, grace Reiter — Twilight (but better). After sending up Panem, Mashable 101 creator Grace Reiter is headed to Forks. The Saturday Night Live cast member and 2026 Mashable 101 honoree is directing and improvising her way through a Twilight parody, her second unscripted feature after The Hunger Games (but better), which drew more than 18 million views. The upcoming one premieres Feb. 18 on Reiter's channel.

Industry observers note that aryna Sabalenka — Aryna’s Arena: Unfiltered. What does wedding planning look like when most of the year is spent living out of a suitcase? Sabalenka's new docuseries follows the tennis champion from the tennis tour to dress fittings and brand meetings, including a project to design her own $250,000 diamond necklace. The show expands on her existing YouTube series, Aryna’s Arena, and premieres on her channel in spring 2027.

In a recent development, wesley Wang — Response, Extract 14, and Absolute Cinema. If your group chat is always trying to solve the murder before the big reveal, Extract 14 will give you all something to work with. The six-episode mystery hides clues in found footage and offers $100,000 to the first viewer who cracks the case. Wang also has Response, a sci-fi horror short about park rangers who find something unsettling during a welfare check, and Absolute Cinema, which brings 10 aspiring filmmakers to New York for a weeklong boot camp. Viewers get the final say on who wins $100,000 to make their movie. Response is due in early 2027, with the other two projects following in the spring.

Nick DiGiovanni — Chef. Nick DiGiovanni went from MasterChef finalist to YouTube food star, building an audience with step-by-step recipes and stunts like making the world’s largest sushi roll. Now he's turning the camera on other chefs. His newly introduced channel, Chef, takes viewers inside Michelin-starred restaurants and street-food kitchens, with full-length episodes about the people behind the food and daily recipe Shorts filmed from the cook’s POV. The first two videos are already live: a visit to a pizza restaurant and a quick lesson in making butter chicken shawarma.

Morgan Jay — Music Therapy with Morgan Jay. Comedian, musician, and 2025 Mashable 101 cover star Morgan Jay is bringing his musical improv to the therapist's couch. In each episode, he plays therapist to a celebrity guest, and whatever comes up in their unscripted conversation becomes material for an original song they write and perform together. The first season’s guests include Mara Wilson, Yung Gravy, Ron Funches, and Josh Johnson. The series premiered Nov. 18 on Jay's YouTube channel.

The slate also includes Lilly Singh's Eligible Aunties, a dating series about older single women, and Track Star Tonight, a live music series from the team behind Jack Coyne's street quiz. Scott Evans heads to Lagos, Nigeria, for the Jan. 8 premiere of House Guest Vacay. Before then, Happy Hour with Ina Garten has a Thanksgiving special on Nov. 25, and Sam Eckholm goes behind the scenes with the Royal Air Force's Red Arrows on the Nov. 27 episode of Access Granted. Latest episodes of the docuseries Created with Jon Youshaei are also due this winter. That's a lot of new, original content!

YouTube has been working on two things a recurring show needs.

It has been revealed that the first is a way for viewers to find the next episode. Creators can organize longer videos into seasons and episodes, and in September, YouTube revealed a similar feature for Shorts, allowing viewers to watch them in order.

The second is a way to find sponsors. In March, YouTube introduced Creator Partnerships, which connects creators in YouTube Studio with marketers using Google’s ad tools. At the showcase, YouTube pointed to NYX's takeover of Mashable 101 star Brittany Broski's Royal Court and Expedia's partnership with another Mashable 101 creator, iShowSpeed.

One of the clearest examples is a show that aired for eight seasons on Netflix. Phil Rosenthal's Somebody Feed Phil will premiere its ninth season on his own YouTube channel this spring. United Airlines is the title sponsor and looks to carry the series on its in-flight screens, giving the show yet another place to reach viewers.

From YouTubers and TikTok stars to streamers and podcasters, Mashable talks to creators about how they built their platforms, the gear they swear by, and the trends they see coming next.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Everful, a San Francisco- and Singapore-based startup that connects smaller retailers and brands with Chinese factories and manages the process from order to delivery, has raised $48.5 million in Series A funding.
  • The round was led by Vertex Ventures Southeast Asia & India and January Capital, with participation from existing investors Square Peg and Lightspeed.
  • In a recent development, song, a former Alibaba executive, and serial entrepreneur Kevin Han, who sold a previous company to Amazon, co-founded Everful in 2024.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Everful, a San Francisco- and Singapore-based startup that connects smaller retailers and brands with Chinese factories and manages the process from order to delivery, has raised $48.5 million in Series A funding.

The round was led by Vertex Ventures Southeast Asia & India and January Capital, with participation from existing investors Square Peg and Lightspeed.

In a recent development, song, a former Alibaba executive, and serial entrepreneur Kevin Han, who sold a previous company to Amazon, co-founded Everful in 2024. The company began as a jewelry wholesale business before evolving into a multi-category, factory-direct sourcing platform.

According to recent reports, retailers and brands often rely on intermediaries, face high minimum order requirements, and experience long sourcing cycles, which tie up capital in inventory before sales trends are clear. Song noticed the growing gap between fast-changing consumer trends and traditional wholesale sourcing models while working as a venture investor at Bessemer Venture Partners, where she mostly focused on cross-border sourcing and meeting numerous startups in the sector. That same gap shaped Everful’s goal to simplify buying directly from factories through an AI-enabled platform.

The B2B sourcing industry is highly competitive. Major Tech giant Alibaba connects international buyers with manufacturers and suppliers, while Faire, a San Francisco-based wholesale tech platform, enables retailers to purchase wholesale inventory directly from brands. According to Everful’s co-founders, its key differentiator is responsibility for the sourcing process, rather than simply facilitating transactions.

“We take care of everything,” Han remarked. “We handle sourcing, order consolidation, quality control, and logistics. That’s something the marketplaces don’t offer.”.

Recent findings suggest that everful is built for smaller retailers and brands without dedicated sourcing teams, Song said, and it also verifies the factories it works with. While peers also offer services such as quality inspection, logistics, and AI-powered sourcing, Everful aims to integrate these capabilities into a more streamlined purchasing experience, creating an end-to-end process that reduces the work retailers must handle themselves.

Han added that Everful uses AI agents to automate labor-intensive sourcing tasks, including tracking consumer trends, identifying suppliers, coordinating orders across factories, and managing logistics.

Because Everful sources from Chinese factories, ongoing U.S.-China trade tensions and tariffs bear directly on its business. Song mentioned the co-founders have been thinking about geopolitical challenges since day one of building the tech giant, and that this has shaped Everful’s strategy from the outset, leveraging her experience at Alibaba and Bessemer Venture Partners.

She mentioned the Trump administration’s suspension of the de minimis exemption, which had allowed eligible shipments valued at $800 or less to enter the U.S. duty-free, as one example of a shift in trade policy.

Song explained such changes could favor a model that combines overseas sourcing with local retail sales. “We’re empowering local retailers and brands,” she said. “Long-term cross-border commerce will be cross-border B2B sourcing plus local selling.”.

Everful plans to use the Series A round to expand its presence in the U.S. and Europe, particularly the U.K., France, and Italy, while investing in AI to automate product customization and other sourcing workflows. It also aims to deepen integrations with e-commerce platforms, building on its Shopify integration as it works toward becoming an end-to-end infrastructure platform for global sourcing.

The startup employs about 70 full-time staff globally, including 45 in research and development. It has also established an AI operations team to connect engineering and business functions.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • You can do this on Xbox Series X and PlayStation 5.
  • Even if you've been eagerly awaiting the release of Grand Theft Auto 6, shelling out $80 for the standard edition or $100 for the ultimate edition isn't easy for everyone.
  • Sources indicate that both Xbox Series X and PlayStation 5 have a game sharing feature that lets you play one copy of a game on two different consoles.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

You can do this on Xbox Series X and PlayStation 5.

Even if you've been eagerly awaiting the release of Grand Theft Auto 6, shelling out $80 for the standard edition or $100 for the ultimate edition isn't easy for everyone. You shouldn't expect the biggest game of the year to go on sale any time soon, but the good news is there's another way to save some money on it. The only catch is that you need a friend who wants to play the game on the same kind of console and is willing to split the cost with you.

Sources indicate that both Xbox Series X and PlayStation 5 have a game sharing feature that lets you play one copy of a game on two different consoles. While there are some restrictions on sharing DLC and other in-game items, most full games can be shared, and GTA 6 is no exception.

Industry observers note that on PlayStation 5, sharing works by signing into your account on two different consoles and enabling the console sharing feature. After buying GTA 6, sign into your PlayStation account on the console you want to share the game with. Open Settings on the console's main screen, then go to Users and Accounts and select Other. Open Console Sharing and Offline Play and toggle the feature on.

While logged into your account, your friend can now download any of your games to their own console, then switch back to their own account to play the game. Keep in mind that your account can only share games with one other console at a time. Your friend will also need to remember to switch back to their own account after starting to download one of your games, since you can't use the same account on two consoles simultaneously. Once you've set up console sharing, your friend will maintain access to your library permanently unless you change your password.

This will allow anyone using this Xbox to download games on your account without you signing in. In the menu itself, a note recommends making your own console your home Xbox, but that would only allow another user to play GTA 6 on your own console. Also note that you can only switch your home Xbox five times per year, so be mindful of that limit if you want to change who you're sharing games with.

Meta employees have raised concerns that the company’s AI agent Muse has been mixing up conversations across different accounts and exposing private user data, according to a upcoming Reuters report that looked at internal company posts.

In some of these instances, employees said Muse surfaced messages about childcare requests they never made, career advice they never asked for, product orders they never placed, and bank account balances that didn’t belong to them.

One employee told colleagues that Muse had randomly sent an extra message in a chat about weather and tide information, saying: “BTW, two bank updates, your Capital One balance is $2722.58, your Charles Schwab balance is $5899.57.”.

In another example, an employee using the AI agent on her personal phone received a reminder from Muse to respond to a message from her sister on Signal, the popular end-to-end encrypted messaging app.

Industry observers note that “This seems like an extreme privacy violation. I definitely did not grant it access to other apps, or recall being asked about this,” the employee remarked in her post, according to the report.

“Employee testing is core to the product development process and the entire point is to get feedback, so we can implement safety and privacy protections and improve products,” a Meta spokesperson said in an email to TechCrunch. “Importantly, employees have access to different versions of Muse than the public, so they’re often reviewing features, functionality, and behavior not available elsewhere.”.

Launched in September, Muse is one of the fastest-growing apps on record, with more than 10 million downloads.

“Let’s take software engineering. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nvidia's deepening sell-off following last week's leadership shake-up is overwhelming the optimism surrounding Anthropic's stock market debut and hurting the rest of the artificial intelligence trade, CNBC's Jim Cramer argued Thursday.

The Claude creator raised a record-breaking $81.3 billion, and shares surged as high as $115 in their trading debut Thursday. While off the highs of the session, the stock closed up 17% from its IPO price of $83. But the excitement did little to lift the broader market, with the Nasdaq Composite and S&P 500 both falling roughly 2%. Nvidia, once the beating heart of the AI trade, dropped 3.3% for its sixth straight day of losses — a skid that began Nov. 12, the day longtime CEO Jensen Huang's abrupt resignation was declared amid a widening affair scandal.

Cramer argued that Nvidia's continued decline is dragging down other technology stocks, wiping out wealth faster than Anthropic's blockbuster debut can create it.

"Nvidia is casting a pall on the market that's tainting everything," the "Mad Money" host said.

Sources indicate that despite reporting blockbuster earnings earlier this week, with revenue more than doubling from a year earlier and beating expectations, Nvidia has struggled to regain investors' confidence in the wake of Huang's exit. Shares have fallen 16% since his resignation.

Cramer argued that Huang's desire to return could further complicate Nvidia's search for a permanent CEO. Any successor would face the challenge of leading a company still closely associated with its founder, raising questions about whether a latest chief executive could establish authority while Huang remains influential. Nvidia's board noted it is not considering bringing back Huang.

The continued chatter about a potential Huang return "makes it so that this still-giant tech giant is sinking like a stone, destroying the savings of millionaires and regular index investors alike," Cramer mentioned.

The damage extends well beyond Nvidia itself. As the longtime leader of the AI trade, the chipmaker has helped drive investor enthusiasm for everything from semiconductor manufacturers to data center infrastructure companies. Its continued decline is now weighing on those same stocks, Cramer mentioned, cutting against the bullish hope that Anthropic's IPO would revive the rest of the AI trade.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that if you’re still using your iPhone’s “Radar” sound as an alarm, it might be time for an upgrade. The latest Hatch Sleep Clock is designed to make both falling asleep and waking up a little more pleasant. It combines a sunrise alarm clock, dimmable bedside light, sound machine, and contactless sleep tracking into one bedside gadget. And for the first time, it’s going on sale (early) as a Black Friday deal.

From November 19 through November 20, the Sleep Clock is 25 percent off at Hatch and Amazon. Normally $250, it’s down to $188, which is just $18 more than the Hatch Restore 3’s $170 retail price. And unlike its predecessor, the newer Hatch adds passive sleep monitoring, which is pretty compelling for anyone who hates wearing wearables to bed. Or maybe you’re like me and occasionally forget to wear your Oura Ring to bed, in which case, you wouldn’t have to worry because the Hatch is already quietly tracking your sleep in the background.

I’ve been testing the Hatch Sleep Clock for over two months, and it’s earned a permanent spot on my nightstand. As someone who already wears a smart ring and smartwatch to bed, I’m not exactly short on sleep-tracking data. But I’ve never owned a sunrise alarm clock, and I instantly became a convert. Unlike my iPhone or Amazon Echo Dot, it doesn’t wake me up by blaring an obnoxious alarm in my pitch-black bedroom. Instead, it gradually illuminates the room within my scheduled wake-up time. You can customize the sunrise's duration and brightness, and pair it with a soundscape of your choosing. It truly makes getting out of bed feel less jarring, especially as the mornings get darker.

Most notably, the Sleep Clock also doubles as a contactless sleep tracker, using a built-in motion sensor to detect your movements and breathing throughout the night. I compared its readings against my Oura Ring 5 and Apple Watch Series 12, and while sleep duration estimates were generally aligned, the sleep-stage readings were less consistent. The device doesn’t measure physiological metrics like heart rate, and it can’t detect snoring or other audio-based sleep disruptions. I also found that placement significantly matters. My nightstand tends to collect clutter, so I had to rearrange my trinkets to make room for the clock.

Each morning, the Hatch app gives you a breakdown of when you went to bed, when you fell asleep, when you woke up, and how much time you spent in different sleep stages. The color-coded reports are easy to understand without burying me in random metrics. Plus, unlike most sleep trackers, Hatch doesn't require a subscription to access your sleep data. (You will need that Hatch+ membership ($6 per month) if you want to access the full audio library, however.).

Recent findings suggest that overall, the Hatch Sleep Clock is the best all-in-one bedside device. I wouldn’t recommend replacing your dedicated wearable with it if detailed health tracking is your priority. But if you’ve been wanting a sunrise alarm clock that can also offer a little insight into your sleep, do not sleep on this Black Friday deal.

If you don’t care for sleep tracking, Hatch is also offering discounts on several other products across its lineup.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • In a recent development, the tech giant is a little late to the game with this launch, as other leading AI model makers like OpenAI, Anthropic, and Meta have already been offering agentic features in their desktop applications for some time.
